content_groups.group_title: Q: Why do you use a speculum?

blocks.text: To visualize the vaginal walls and cervix and to identify abnormalities or obtain appropriate samples.

content_groups.group_title: Q: What is a Cusco's speculum?

blocks.text: A self-retaining bivalve vaginal speculum used to visualize the vagina and cervix.

content_groups.group_title: Q: What do you look for on the cervix?

blocks.text: Eversion of the endocervical columnar epithelium onto the ectocervix, producing a reddish appearance around the external os. It can be associated with pregnancy and hormonal states and may cause discharge or contact bleeding.

content_groups.group_title: Q: What causes a friable cervix?
Q: What is a strawberry cervix?

blocks.text: A punctate erythematous cervical appearance classically associated with Trichomonas vaginalis infection.

content_groups.group_title: Q: What would you look for if you suspect ruptured membranes?

blocks.text: Pooling of fluid in the vagina/posterior fornix and fluid passing through the cervix, while assessing the colour and characteristics of the fluid.

content_groups.group_title: Q: What does green liquor suggest?
Q: What would foul-smelling liquor suggest?

blocks.text: Possible intra-amniotic infection, particularly when associated with maternal fever, uterine tenderness or fetal/maternal tachycardia.
